clips.send: Respecting and protecting human rights. “The state respects and protects human rights.”. The textbook defines human rights as the rights a person should have as a human being; their goal is each person’s free and all-round development. This sentence was written into the Constitution in 2004 and is a constitutional principle. Who has them: every citizen — with special care for women, minors, the elderly and people with disabilities. What they cover: equality, political rights, personal freedom, and economic, social, cultural and educational rights.

clips.send: All power belongs to the people. “All power in the People’s Republic of China belongs to the people.”. The Constitution describes China as a socialist state under the people’s democratic dictatorship, led by the working class and based on the alliance of workers and peasants. The people use their power through the people’s congresses: the national one (NPC) and local ones at every level. People also take part in running state, economic, cultural and social affairs in ways the law provides.

clips.send: The Constitution. The fundamental law of the state, with supreme legal force. Content: it sets out the most basic questions of national life. Force: it is the strongest law. Other laws are written on its basis and may not go against it. Procedure: it is harder to change than any other law (two thirds of all NPC deputies). The textbook calls it “the general charter for governing the country”.

clips.send: Supervising the Constitution. “The life of the Constitution lies in its implementation, and so does its authority.”. The NPC and its Standing Committee have the power to supervise how the Constitution is carried out. No law or regulation may go against the Constitution; rules that do are reviewed and corrected. Every act that breaks the Constitution or the laws must be investigated. No organisation or person has the privilege of being above the Constitution and the laws.

clips.send: Laws. Ordinary laws are written on the basis of the Constitution and fill in its details. The National People’s Congress (全国人民代表大会, NPC) and its Standing Committee make China’s national laws. Many laws open with the line “This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution”. Examples: the Civil Code, the Criminal Law, the Compulsory Education Law, the Law on the Protection of Minors.

clips.send: Administrative regulations. Rules made by the State Council in line with the Constitution and the laws. The State Council (国务院, Guówùyuàn) is the central government and the highest administrative organ. Examples: the Regulations on School Bus Safety; the Regulations on Protecting Minors Online. They may not go against the Constitution or the laws.

clips.send: Rules for state power. The Constitution sets up the state organs and sets rules for how they use power. Power belongs to the people; the Constitution creates state organs and gives each its job. State power must stay inside the limits set by the Constitution and the laws. It must be used lawfully: “duties set by law must be done; without legal authority, nothing may be done.”. The purpose: regulate state power in order to protect citizens’ rights.

clips.send: Constitution Day and the oath. 4 December is National Constitution Day in China. The current Constitution was adopted on 4 December 1982; since 2014 that date is National Constitution Day. Schools hold readings and class meetings about the Constitution that day. State officials must publicly swear an oath to the Constitution when they take office (宪法宣誓, xiànfǎ xuānshì). The oath begins: “I pledge to be loyal to the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China, safeguard its authority and perform my legal duties…”

clips.send: Local regulations. Rules for one region, made to fit local conditions. Made by the people’s congresses (and their standing committees) of provinces, autonomous regions, the four big municipalities, and cities divided into districts. Example: one city’s rules on sorting household rubbish. They may not go against the Constitution, the laws or administrative regulations — if one does, it can be corrected or cancelled.

clips.send: 宪法。宪法是国家的根本法，具有最高的法律效力。从内容上看：宪法规定国家生活中的根本问题。从效力上看：宪法具有最高的法律效力，是其他法律的立法基础和立法依据，其他法律不得与宪法相抵触。从制定和修改程序上看：宪法比其他法律更为严格（须全国人大全体代表的三分之二以上多数通过）。宪法是治国安邦的总章程，是党和人民意志的集中体现。

clips.send: 规范国家权力运行。宪法组织国家机构，规范国家权力的运行。权力属于人民；宪法设立国家机构，并授予其相应的职权。国家权力必须在宪法和法律限定的范围内行使。国家权力必须依法行使：法定职责必须为，法无授权不可为。我国国家机构实行民主集中制原则。宪法的核心价值追求：规范国家权力运行以保障公民权利。

clips.send: 国家的一切权力属于人民。我国宪法规定：“中华人民共和国的一切权力属于人民。”。我国是工人阶级领导的、以工农联盟为基础的人民民主专政的社会主义国家。人民行使国家权力的机关是全国人民代表大会和地方各级人民代表大会。人民依照法律规定，通过各种途径和形式，管理国家事务，管理经济和文化事业，管理社会事务。宪法确认公民享有广泛的权利，并为实现这些权利提供保障。

clips.send: 地方性法规。结合本地实际制定，在本行政区域内有效。由省、自治区、直辖市和设区的市的人民代表大会及其常务委员会制定。例如：某市的生活垃圾管理条例。地方性法规不得同宪法、法律、行政法规相抵触；如有抵触，可以通过备案审查予以纠正或撤销。

clips.send: 国家宪法日与宪法宣誓。每年12月4日是国家宪法日。现行宪法于1982年12月4日通过并公布施行；2014年，全国人大常委会决定将12月4日设立为国家宪法日。国家工作人员就职时应当依照法律规定公开进行宪法宣誓。誓词开头是：“我宣誓：忠于中华人民共和国宪法，维护宪法权威，履行法定职责……”。中学生要学习宪法、认同宪法、践行宪法。

clips.send: 加强宪法监督。宪法的生命在于实施，宪法的权威也在于实施。全国人大及其常委会行使监督宪法实施的职权。一切法律、行政法规和地方性法规都不得同宪法相抵触；要推进合宪性审查工作，加强备案审查。一切违反宪法和法律的行为，必须予以追究。任何组织或者个人都不得有超越宪法和法律的特权。

clips.send: 法律。普通法律依据宪法制定，是对宪法的具体化。全国人民代表大会和全国人民代表大会常务委员会行使国家立法权。许多法律第一条都写明“根据宪法，制定本法”。例如：《民法典》《刑法》《义务教育法》《未成年人保护法》。普通法律规定国家生活中某一方面的问题，不得与宪法相抵触。

clips.send: 尊重和保障人权。我国宪法规定：“国家尊重和保障人权。”。人权是指人作为人应当享有的权利，其实质内容和目标是人自由、全面地发展。尊重和保障人权是我国的宪法原则（2004年宪法修正案写入）。人权的主体非常广泛：全体公民，包括妇女、未成年人、老年人、残疾人等特殊群体。人权的内容非常广泛：平等权、政治权利、人身自由，以及社会经济、文化教育方面的权利等。
